android.icon_token: Core populates icon_token in six places and no shell renders any of them. The values are SF Symbol names, so the vocabulary has to be decided before a non-Apple shell can map them — see backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.

ios.icon_token: Core populates icon_token in six places and no shell renders any of them. The values are SF Symbol names, so the vocabulary has to be decided before a non-Apple shell can map them — see backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.

linux-gtk.detail: Real gap. Core populates detail on three row builders (contact status, settings values, link details) and it is never shown. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
linux-gtk.enabled: Dormant, not dropped: every PresentationRow Core builds hardcodes `enabled: true`, so no shell can be observed honouring it. Revisit when Core first emits a disabled row — a shell that ignores it would then let the user activate something Core disabled, and this exemption would hide that.
linux-gtk.fallback_text: Real gap. The initials fallback is plain text and every shell can render it, including a terminal — Android was fixed for exactly this and now draws the initials circle. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
linux-gtk.icon_token: Core populates icon_token in six places and no shell renders any of them. The values are SF Symbol names, so the vocabulary has to be decided before a non-Apple shell can map them — see backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
linux-gtk.image_data: Real gap for a graphical shell. Core sends avatar bytes; iOS and Android draw them. A terminal cannot, which is why the TUI entry is narrower — see fallback_text there. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.

tui.accessibility: Real gap. Core prepares the accessibility label for every row and this shell never reads it, so assistive tech gets nothing for a row. Worst on linux-gtk, where AT-SPI is the whole a11y surface. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
tui.controls: Settings toggles are unreachable in the TUI for the same reason. A terminal can render a checkbox, so this is a gap rather than a platform limit.
tui.detail: Real gap. Core populates detail on three row builders (contact status, settings values, link details) and it is never shown. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
tui.enabled: Dormant, not dropped: every PresentationRow Core builds hardcodes `enabled: true`, so no shell can be observed honouring it. Revisit when Core first emits a disabled row — a shell that ignores it would then let the user activate something Core disabled, and this exemption would hide that.
tui.fallback_text: Not a gap for a terminal. The fallback is initials standing in for an avatar, and the row title is already the name they are derived from — rendering "AL Alice" adds noise, not information. The generic "every shell can draw text" reasoning was too broad here; it holds for the graphical shells, which is where this stays a real gap.
tui.icon_token: Core populates icon_token in six places and no shell renders any of them. The values are SF Symbol names, so the vocabulary has to be decided before a non-Apple shell can map them — see backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
tui.image_data: Not a gap for a terminal: a TUI cannot draw avatar bytes at all, and the initials substitute adds nothing beside the name — see fallback_text above.
tui.secondary_actions: Real gap. Core populates per-row actions from item.actions; a shell that drops them leaves those actions unreachable. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
tui.selected: Real gap. Core computes selected from field visibility on two row builders, so it is not always false — a shell that ignores it shows the wrong row as chosen. Tracked in backlog/2026-08-20-core-prepares-presentation-data-no-shell-renders.
